sentences.text: Gurmukh Singh vs State Of Uttarakhand on 14 March, 2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
 High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.175 of 2024
Gurmukh Singh ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Present:-
Mr. M.K. Ray, Advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant Gurmukh Singh, is in judicial custody in Fir No. 111 of 2023, under Section 363, 366, 376
(2) Ipc and Section 5l /6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police
Station Kelakhera, District Udham Singh Nagar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the victim, a minor girl was enticed by the applicant.
It is a prosecution case that subsequently, the victim was recovered.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the victim is not a child.
She is major.
Her date of birth as per Aadhar Card is 02.01.2005.
She wanted to marry the applicant.
She has left her house on her own.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 ("the Code"), she has not stated anything about physical relations.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that as per school record, date of birth of the victim is 02.09.2005.

She would submit that the victim has supported the prosecution case during investigation, but she admits that in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code, the victim has not stated anything about physical relations with the applicant.
6. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
